question: What if Showdown gave the battle the whole screen?
name: Pokémon Showdown Restyler
what: A Tampermonkey script for the new Pokémon Showdown client. The battle field scales up past its old 640 by 360 box, the panes resize, the team sheet and chat get panels of their own, you can pin several side tabs at once, and there’s a light, dark or auto theme. Every part is a module you can switch off.
useWhen: You play on a big monitor and the battle sits in a little box.
You want Showdex, chat and the team sheet on screen at the same time.
You stream and want a cleaner layout.
thenAsk: How do you change a website you don’t own? With a script that runs on top of it.
Why wrap the page’s own functions instead of replacing them?
What panel would you add through its API?

detail.lede: The Pokémon Showdown Restyler. A bigger battle, panes you can drag, chat and team sheets in their own panels, and a modern theme, built from small modules you can turn on and off.

what.title: Same Showdown, more room.
body: The stock client keeps the battle in a small box and stacks everything else in one side panel. The Restyler gives the field room to grow and lets you put the things you watch side by side.
Drag the slider to compare the stock client with the restyled one.

how.title: Install it once, tweak it forever.

steps.title: Install it
steps.body: Add Tampermonkey, open the latest release and click showdown-restyler.user.js. It updates itself from there.

steps.title: Open the new client
steps.body: It works on the new Showdown client. On the classic one it stays out of the way.

steps.title: Make it yours
steps.body: Drag the bar between the battle and the side panel, drop side tabs where you want them, and open the gear for every option.

how.headsUp: The new client changes often, so an update on Showdown’s side can break something. Turning a module off puts that part back to stock.

works.title: Wrap, don’t replace.
body: Showdown has no plugin system, so the script wraps the client’s own functions: it adds its bit and then calls the original. Every patch can be undone, which is how each module switches off cleanly and why it can share the page with Showdex.
Other scripts get a small API to add panels of their own.
works.callout: this is the whole API, really

ideas.title: Where you could take it next.

items.title: A theme editor
items.body: The client hard-codes about 170 colors with no CSS variables. Map them to tokens and anyone could paint their own skin.

items.title: Theme presets
items.body: Save a whole skin as JSON and pass it to a friend, using the export the settings already have.

items.title: A panel of your own
items.body: A timer, a damage note, a scouting list. One registerPanel call puts it next to the battle.
